purpose: Establish which reproducible operating point the repository's own fp_budget=2 rule implies, and how far the DEPLOYED frozen threshold is from it. Written in response to audit-1 D1.
ratio_note: the brief specifies ~7:3 (real:fake); the shipped set is 47:53 (56 ai / 63 real), so both are reported
threshold_space: logits; probability = sigmoid(logit). Thresholds are stored at full float64 precision -- rounding the rule-implied threshold to 6 dp (-0.424307) makes it LARGER than the 3rd largest pooled real score (-0.4243068333333333) and admits 3 positives instead of 2.
rule_definition: admit at most 2 real samples -> threshold must be strictly below the 3rd largest pooled pure-real fused score, i.e. thr in (4th_largest, 3rd_largest]; implementing it as 3rd_largest + 1e-12 puts the admitted count at exactly 2.

finding.conclusion: The DEPLOYED frozen threshold (thr_high=0.826623) is NOT the point the repository's own stated rule (fp_budget=2 on pooled pure-real scores) implies. The rule implies -0.424307, which realises 97.48% pooled / 96.08% per-round accuracy at the SAME FP count (2/63) and strictly dominates the deployed threshold. The published 95.94% matches neither and is not reproducible from repo/models/.
finding.fpr_requirement: NOTE: 2/63 = 3.17% still EXCEEDS the required <=3%. On this set satisfying <=3% requires at most 1 FP (1.59%), and every threshold reaching 0 FP destroys recall (accuracy ~53%), so <=3% is not met by any reproducible operating point.

caveat: The pooled score is a diagnostic aggregate, not a deployable per-item rule. Per-round application of the rule-implied threshold yields FP counts of 2-5, i.e. the bound holds in aggregate, not uniformly per round.
